text:
jana_support: FYI customer ACME hit a sudden billing spike + intermittent 503s after a SCIM deprov yesterday evening. They also saw KMS decrypt failures in app logs. Opening thread to triage.

mike_cse: thanks jana. do we have customer tenant id + repro steps? any recent deploys? :eyes:

jana_support: tenant_id: acme-prod-42. They say deprovisioned ~2026-02-28T22:10Z. Short repro they sent: 1) remove user via SCIM 2) call embeddings endpoint for existing session 3) get 503s + billing jump. Logs they pasted: ```
ERROR: api: write response failed: 503 Service Unavailable
2026-02-28T22:11:05Z request_id=abc123 path=/v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-v1 err="kms: decrypt: access denied"
```

leo_infra: I pulled traces for acme-prod-42. There's a burst of retries from frontend to runtime around 22:11Z leading to tail latency spike and gateway 503s. trace link: https://traces.prod.redwood/trace/0a1b2c. Looks like runtime returned 500 while attempting to fetch KV cache after a failed decrypt.

anya_security: tagging in. Need a full audit export (SCIM/Provisioning + KMS access logs) for the 22:00-22:20Z window. Also need to confirm whether the SCIM deprov removed access to the key policy or service principal.

priya_billing: I'll pull the usage breakdown for that tenant/time window (tokens, embeddings, retries). Can you confirm which routes were charged? embeddings vs completion?

jana_support: customer reported embeddings were the main workload. they saw 3x normal token usage in that 15m window. they suspect retries doubled counts.

mike_cse: can someone paste exact client request headers and any auth error returned to client? that helps confirm if it's legit retry loop.

leo_infra: here's the snippet from runtime stderr (sanitized): ```
[2026-02-28T22:11:05Z] runtime: session=sev123 shard=3 model=redwood-embed-v1 err="kms: decrypt: access denied for key projects/teams/acme/keys/enc-01"
[2026-02-28T22:11:05Z] runtime: fallback to model-quant-v1 allowed=false, returning 500
[2026-02-28T22:11:06Z] gateway: upstream returned 500, client sees 503, retry scheduled
```

anya_security: that error is consistent with the service principal losing KMS decrypt permission. Two possibilities: 1) SCIM deprov removed a service account group that was in key policy, or 2) an admin rotated keys without updating runtime role. We need the KMS key policy snapshot and SCIM delta for the deprov event.

mike_cse: customer claims they only removed a single user. they didn't rotate keys. can we run a quick query: who removed that user and what did the SCIM delta contain?

jana_support: SCIM system log: ```
2026-02-28T22:09:50Z patch /scim/v2/Users id=U-333 action=delete by=admin@acme corp
2026-02-28T22:09:51Z scim-sync: removed groups [acme-engineers, acme-embedding-service] from user U-333
```

leo_infra: aha — the sync removed membership from acme-embedding-service. That group maps to the runtime service principal used by their infra. If the SCIM mapping incorrectly tied the runtime account to a user instead of a machine identity, deprov will remove its group membership.

anya_security: escalation: this looks like an access control mapping bug. We should: 1) produce audit export (SCIM events + KMS admin audit + key policy snapshots) 2) check for least-privilege misbindings (groups mapped to runtime roles) 3) advise customer on moving machine/service principals to SCIM service-accounts or using SCIM exclusion rules. I'll take point on audit.

priya_billing: billing note: retries being charged will show up as repeated request_ids. if we can correlate request_id pattern we can offer a one-time credits adjustment. please collect request ids from logs.

jana_support: I collected sample request_ids: abc123, abc124, abc125. sending to priya in DM.

mike_cse: short-term mitigation for customer: 1) re-add the removed group membership for the runtime service principal (if they can) OR 2) rotate to a new service principal + update key policy to include it. Which has lower blast radius?

anya_security: re-adding group membership is fastest but we need to confirm SCIM mapping won't remove it again on the next sync. Better long-term: create a dedicated service account that SCIM does not deprov or mark as excluded from auto-deprovision, and update key policy to reference that identity. We'll draft a runbook.

leo_infra: runtime hotfix idea: detect KMS decrypt errors for a tenant and emit a non-retryable error to gateway so client sees 4xx instead of gateway retrying and inflating billing. That would require a small runtime change — file an RFC?

mike_cse: +1 for non-retryable surface to avoid billing pain. but need to avoid breaking legitimate transient KMS errors. maybe only apply when error string contains "access denied" and audit shows recent SCIM delta.

anya_security: action items: - I will export SCIM delta + KMS admin logs for 22:00-22:20Z and attach to this thread (onya). - Leo, can you get runtime trace + request id list? - Priya, billing will prepare a credits proposal pending logs. - Jana/Mike, coordinate comms with ACME.

kms-audit-bot: Audit export ready: https://safestore.redwood/audit/acme-prod-42/exports/2003456789-scim-kms.zip (expires in 7d)

leo_infra: trace + request ids uploaded here: https://internal.artifacts/acme/2003456789/traces.txt

priya_billing: pulled initial numbers: tokens charged during window = 3.2M (baseline 1.1M), retry count ~1.9x. provisional credit = pending review, estimate ~42% of the spike.

mike_cse: I'll draft a customer note: short explanation + immediate steps to re-add group OR create a service account. Jana please review before send.

jana_support: draft looks good, please add an apology and the attach link to audit export. also include recommended runbook steps.

anya_security: I'll follow up with a short runbook draft in this thread about SCIM -> KMS policy hygiene and least-privilege checks. Starting points: - identify machine vs human identities in SCIM mapping - ensure service accounts are excluded from deprov - prefer explicit key policy references to service principal ARNs - monitor for KMS decrypt errors and alert early

deploy-bot: deploy completed: feature/avoid-retries-toxic-503s -> canary on infra pool in 3h (for discussion, not yet live) :shipit:

jana_support: thanks everyone. I'll keep ACME updated with status and ETA for credits. reopening if we see further errors. :white_check_mark:

anya_security: tagging closure only after audit confirmation and customer remediated mapping.

lana_ops (reacted with :thumbsup:): :thumbsup:
